title: Linkability of submissions across courses and sessions
description: The flow carries stable student id together with course, submission timestamp, login context, and uploaded work file metadata/content. At the portal, these attributes can be linked to correlate the same student across multiple assignments, courses, and submission events, enabling profile building of study behavior and performance-related activity.
assumptions: Assumes the portal stores or can observe repeated submissions and login events tied to the same student identifier.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgement; retrieved context confirms L applies to ExternalEntity->Process flows but does not provide the exact sub-node.

title: Identifiability of the student from submitted data
description: Student id directly identifies the student, and the uploaded assignment may also contain name, writing style, or other identifying content. This makes the student readily identifiable to the receiving process and potentially to personnel or downstream components with access to the submission.
assumptions: Assumes the assignment file or account context is associated with an identifiable student record.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro sub-node id is chosen by best judgement because the retrieved context only establishes applicability at the flow.

title: Insufficient evidence about assignment submission and receipt
description: If the portal does not generate trustworthy proof of submission and receipt, the student could later be unable to demonstrate that a specific file was submitted at a specific time, or the portal could be unable to prove what was received. This creates a privacy-relevant non-repudiation gap around a personal academic action.
assumptions: Assumes submission acknowledgements, immutable timestamps, or receipts may be missing or weak.
uncertainty_note: Sub-node id is approximate; applicability depends on whether auditable receipts already exist.

title: Detectability of student activity from login and submission events
description: The existence of this flow reveals that a particular student is active in the portal and is submitting coursework for a given course at a particular time. Even without accessing full content, observing the flow or its metadata can disclose participation, deadlines behavior, or lateness patterns.
assumptions: Assumes network observers, logs, or internal monitors can observe event occurrence or metadata.
uncertainty_note: Exact sub-node id is best-effort; retrieved context supports detectability on this flow type.

title: Disclosure of sensitive submission contents and metadata
description: The flow contains the work file plus student id, course, and submission timestamp. If transmitted, logged, cached, or exposed without adequate protection, unauthorized parties could access personal data, academic work product, and timing information, potentially revealing performance, special circumstances, or other sensitive details.
assumptions: Assumes there is some risk of inadequate transport protection, excessive logging, or over-broad access within the portal.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is selected by best judgement; context confirms disclosure is applicable at the flow.

title: Unawareness of how submission data will be used, retained, and shared
description: The student may not be adequately informed, at the point of upload, about how the assignment file and related metadata will be processed, how long they will be retained, whether they are shared with instructors, plagiarism-detection services, or support staff, and what visibility others have into timestamps and course activity.
assumptions: Assumes notices or just-in-time explanations in the portal may be incomplete or absent.
uncertainty_note: Applicability is strong for this kind of portal flow, but the specific sub-node id is approximate.

title: Collection of more personal data than necessary for assignment submission
description: The flow includes several attributes beyond the file itself, such as student id and precise submission timestamp, and the file may contain embedded metadata. If the portal collects, retains, or mandates data not necessary for receiving and grading the assignment, it may violate data minimization or purpose-limitation expectations.
assumptions: Assumes some elements of the collected metadata or file metadata are not strictly necessary, or are retained longer than needed.
uncertainty_note: Need for all collected fields cannot be fully verified from the prompt; sub-node id is best-effort.

title: Student identifier in routed request enables direct identification
description: The portal sends student id together with course, file reference, and requesting role to the assignment & grading service. Because the flow contains a unique student identifier, the receiving process can directly identify the data subject when handling submission and grading requests.
assumptions: Assumes 'student id' is unique within the institution and is available to the grading service in clear or otherwise readily attributable form.

title: Assignment and grading service processes identified student data
description: This flow causes the assignment & grading service to process identified data for submissions and grading operations. The combination of student id, course context, and file reference ties educational actions to a specific student.
assumptions: Assumes the service uses these fields to execute grading or submission workflows rather than immediately de-identifying them.

title: Submission and grading requests may create attributable evidence a student cannot later deny
description: Requests carrying student id, course, file reference, and role can become evidence that a particular student submitted work or was associated with a grading-related action. If retained in service logs or audit trails, this may prevent the student from plausibly denying the submission event or related claim about their involvement.
assumptions: Assumes the assignment & grading service logs requests, timestamps, or transaction metadata in a way that preserves attribution to the student.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgment; retrieved context established Nr applicability for Process->Process but did not provide a specific Nr node citation.

title: Assignment behavior may be detectable from routed educational requests
description: The flow reveals that a student associated with a given student id and course is interacting with the assignment and grading function. Observing or accessing this flow at the receiving process can disclose that the student is submitting coursework or is subject to grading activity, which is a detectable event about the individual.
assumptions: Assumes request handling, logs, or metadata at the service expose the occurrence of submission/grading events to parties who otherwise would not know them.
uncertainty_note: Specific D tree node is chosen by best judgment because the retrieved snippets did not include a detectability node list.

title: Educational records are shared for grading without demonstrated purpose limitation or minimization
description: The portal forwards student id, course, file reference, and role to the grading service. If all of these attributes are not strictly necessary for each request, or if the sharing is not transparently justified under the applicable educational/privacy basis, the flow risks non-compliance with data minimization and purpose-limitation obligations.
assumptions: Assumes there may be scenarios where pseudonymous tokens or reduced attributes could suffice, and that compliance obligations such as transparency, purpose limitation, or minimization apply.
uncertainty_note: Node chosen by best judgment; compliance assessment depends on system purpose, notices, and legal basis not provided in the prompt.

title: Excessive retention/storage of identifiable submission metadata
description: The grading service stores the submitted assignment together with direct identifiers and metadata (student id, course, submission time) in the assignment store. If all of these fields are retained in identifiable form without strict necessity, this creates avoidable data disclosure at rest and increases the amount of personal data exposed through normal access, later reuse, or breach.
assumptions: Assumes the full assignment file and associated metadata are stored in DS1 in identifiable form and that not all stored fields or retention duration are strictly necessary for grading purposes.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selection is best-effort based on general LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimality concepts; the retrieved context confirms Dd applies to Process->DataStore but does not provide the exact subtree node text.

title: Linkability of submissions across courses and time
description: Storing assignment content together with student id, course, and precise submission time enables linking multiple submissions to the same student across different courses or periods. This can facilitate profiling of academic behavior beyond the immediate grading purpose.
assumptions: Assumes DS1 permits records to be queried or correlated using student id and/or timestamps across multiple submissions.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro subtree id may differ; applicability of linkability is strong given the explicit persistent identifier and metadata in the same store.

title: Identifiability of the student from stored assignment record
description: The stored record contains a direct identifier (student id) alongside course and submission time, making the data subject directly identifiable in the assignment store. If direct identification is not necessary for all storage or processing stages, this is a privacy threat.
assumptions: Assumes student id uniquely identifies a student to system operators or connected systems.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is best-effort; the threat itself clearly applies because a direct identifier is stored.

title: Storage may exceed purpose limitation or data-minimization expectations
description: Persisting the full assignment file plus student id, course, and precise submission time may go beyond what is necessary if some attributes are not required for grading, dispute handling, or mandated retention. This creates a non-compliance risk with purpose limitation, data minimization, and storage limitation principles.
assumptions: Assumes no documented necessity exists for all stored attributes and/or their retention period.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is inferred from LINDDUN non-compliance categories rather than from the retrieved excerpts.

title: Teacher account is directly identified during login and queue request
description: To authenticate the teacher and return the correct course-specific submission queue, the web app processes directly identifying account data and course association data. This creates an identifying threat because the request is explicitly tied to a known teacher identity rather than a pseudonymous session alone.
assumptions: The login/request includes a teacher username, email, employee identifier, or equivalent account identifier.

title: Teacher activity can be linked across login and review-queue requests
description: Repeated queue requests from the same authenticated teacher can be linked together by the web app, allowing construction of a profile of the teacher's teaching assignments, review workload, and activity timing across courses.
assumptions: The portal maintains account/session identifiers and request logs that associate multiple actions with the same teacher.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement; the retrieved context did not include a specific linkability node citation.

title: Login and queue request disclose a teacher's course assignments and work patterns
description: This flow reveals personal information about the teacher to the web app, including which courses they teach, that they are currently performing grading duties, and potentially when they are active. Such observations can disclose behavior and role-related information beyond the minimum needed for authentication if broadly visible internally or logged extensively.
assumptions: The application or supporting infrastructure logs requested course queues, timestamps, and authenticated teacher identity.
uncertainty_note: Exact disclosure subtree node may vary depending on the project's threat-tree version; node selected by best judgement.

title: Teacher may be unable to deny having requested a submissions queue
description: If the web app records authenticated queue-access events with strong attribution to the teacher, those records can later be used as evidence that the teacher accessed certain course submissions at specific times. This creates a non-repudiation/privacy threat because the teacher may have no plausible deniability regarding their access activity.
assumptions: The portal keeps audit logs that bind queue requests to a specific authenticated teacher account.
uncertainty_note: Specific non-repudiation node citation is based on best judgement; retrieved context did not provide the exact subtree.

title: Teacher may not have sufficient awareness or choice about processing of login and queue-access data
description: During login and queue retrieval, the system may process account identifiers, timestamps, course associations, and access logs without clearly informing the teacher or offering meaningful control over secondary uses such as monitoring, analytics, or extended retention. This creates a non-compliance risk if transparency, purpose limitation, or data-minimization obligations are not met.
assumptions: The portal provides limited privacy notice or collects more metadata than strictly necessary for authentication and queue delivery.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance subtree node selected by best judgement because the retrieved context did not include relevant Nc nodes.

title: Excessive disclosure of student identity and submission metadata to the teacher
description: The portal flow displays student names, work content, and submission times to the teacher. If the teacher does not need all of these attributes for the specific task, the flow may disclose more personal data than necessary, including identifiable student information and behavioral metadata.
assumptions: Assumes role- and purpose-based access is not sufficiently scoped, and that some displayed attributes may be unnecessary for all teacher use cases.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement from LINDDUN disclosure threat taxonomy; exact node id may vary by threat-tree version.

title: Teacher may be unaware of the extent of student data shown in the portal
description: Students may not be adequately informed that teachers can view not only submitted work but also their names and precise submission times through the portal. This creates a transparency risk around what personal data is exposed to recipients.
assumptions: Assumes the system's privacy notices or in-context explanations do not clearly state which submission attributes are shown to teachers.
uncertainty_note: Applied as an unawareness/transparency threat on this display flow; exact tree-node numbering may differ across LINDDUN Pro materials.

title: Portal display to teacher may be incompatible with the original purpose or legal basis
description: Showing student submissions, names, and timestamps to the teacher may violate privacy requirements if the sharing exceeds the educational purpose originally specified, lacks an appropriate legal basis, or conflicts with data-minimization and purpose-limitation obligations.
assumptions: Assumes there may be insufficient policy, legal basis, or purpose specification governing which student submission details teachers may access.
uncertainty_note: Included because compliance depends strongly on institutional policy and jurisdiction; exact node id is best-effort.

title: Submission records shown to the teacher may be attributable across contexts
description: Displaying student names together with work content and submission times makes the submission directly attributable to a specific student. If the same identifiers and timing data are reused across courses or activities, the flow can support stronger identification than necessary.
assumptions: Assumes identifiers and timestamps can be correlated with other portal data or teacher-held records.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible identifiability threat inherent in named submissions; exact threat-tree node id is best-effort.

title: Teacher identity exposed with grading action
description: The flow includes grader id together with student id, grade, and feedback. This can reveal which teacher assessed which student work, exposing the teacher's involvement in a specific educational action beyond what may be necessary for transmission.
assumptions: Assumes the grader id is a stable identifier and that unnecessary parties or intermediaries could observe or process the full payload on this flow.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement for identifiability of the sender on the flow; exact node naming may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Teacher could repudiate having submitted a grade or feedback entry
description: If the flow lacks strong submission logging, integrity protection, or proof of origin, a teacher may later deny having recorded a particular grade or written feedback. This undermines accountability and dispute resolution around assessment actions.
assumptions: Assumes the portal does not provide robust authentication binding, tamper-evident audit logs, or signed submission records for grading events.
uncertainty_note: Exact non-repudiation subtree id may differ across threat-tree editions; classification is confident.

title: Grade and feedback contents may be disclosed in transit to the portal
description: The flow carries personal data about a student (student id, grade, feedback text) and teacher-related data (grader id). If transmission is not adequately protected, network observers, intermediaries, or unauthorized components could access sensitive educational records and free-text comments.
assumptions: Assumes inadequate transport encryption, weak endpoint protections, or excessive exposure of the payload to intermediaries.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id chosen as a generic disclosure-on-data-flow node based on best judgement.

title: Excessive submission metadata could enable detection of teacher grading activity
description: Even apart from the content itself, observing the timing, frequency, and presence of grade-submission events to the portal can reveal when a teacher is grading, how often assessments are performed, or that a particular student has just been assessed. Such observability can expose sensitive academic workflow patterns.
assumptions: Assumes traffic or application-event visibility by parties able to observe the portal or network metadata.
uncertainty_note: Applies to detectability of the interaction/event; exact tree-node numbering may vary.

title: Student and teacher records may become linkable across assessments
description: The combination of stable student id and grader id in repeated grading submissions allows the portal or other recipients of the flow to correlate multiple assignments, feedback entries, and grading events to the same student-teacher pair. This can enable broader profiling of performance and grading behavior than needed for a single submission.
assumptions: Assumes identifiers are persistent across submissions and that correlation is possible across transactions.
uncertainty_note: Linkability is strongly applicable; exact subtree id is based on best judgement.

title: Grade and feedback may be processed without sufficient notice or policy transparency
description: The flow contains personal data whose collection and use may not be fully transparent to the teacher or student, especially if written feedback is reused for analytics, retention beyond the course, quality monitoring, or sharing with additional roles. Lack of clear notice or communicated policy creates non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes the system may not clearly inform relevant data subjects about purposes, retention, access, and downstream use of grading data.
uncertainty_note: This is a policy/transparency-based non-compliance threat inferred from the data type and flow, so applicability depends on the actual governance context.

title: Grade records in the database are directly identifiable via student ID
description: The grading service stores grade records containing a student id together with course, grade, feedback, grader id, and timestamp. Persisting a direct identifier in the grade-record store makes each record attributable to a specific student and enables identity disclosure to anyone with access to DS2 beyond what is necessary.
assumptions: Assumes DS2 stores the listed fields in directly readable form and is accessible to administrators, support staff, or other internal actors who may not need student identity for every use.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best-fit LINDDUN Pro identification categorization for direct identifiers; exact sub-node naming may vary by repository/version.

title: Longitudinal linking of student performance across courses and time
description: Because DS2 stores student id, course, grade, grader id, and timestamp together, records can be linked across multiple courses and grading events to build a longitudinal profile of a student's academic performance and interactions over time.
assumptions: Assumes repeated writes for the same student accumulate in DS2 and can be queried or correlated.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit tree node for linkability across records; exact sub-node id may differ in some LINDDUN Pro threat trees.

title: Stored grade records enable profiling of student academic performance
description: The combination of student id, course history, grades, feedback, grader id, and timestamps supports inference of performance trends, struggling subjects, and assessment patterns. This creates a detectability/discoverability risk that sensitive educational characteristics become apparent from the stored data.
assumptions: Assumes users or analysts with access to DS2 can search, aggregate, or inspect stored grade data.
uncertainty_note: This is a best-fit use of LINDDUN detectability/discoverability for making sensitive attributes apparent from stored records; exact node id may vary.

title: Unauthorized parties can learn confidential educational data from persisted grade records
description: Grade, qualitative feedback, and associated identifiers are confidential education records. Writing them into DS2 creates a disclosure risk if the datastore is accessed by unauthorized internal users, external attackers, backups, logs, or downstream integrations without sufficient access control or encryption.
assumptions: Assumes no additional safeguards are guaranteed by the flow description.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro disclosure sub-node may differ; selected as best-fit for confidentiality loss of stored personal data.

title: The database write may not provide privacy-relevant proof of who entered or changed a grade
description: Although the grade record includes a grader id and timestamp, the flow description does not indicate tamper-evident logging, authentication binding, or signed audit trails for the write to DS2. A grader or administrator could later deny having created or modified a grade record, undermining accountability for processing personal data.
assumptions: Assumes grader id/timestamp fields are application-supplied and not independently protected against alteration.
uncertainty_note: Applies if the system lacks strong non-repudiation controls; if tamper-evident audit mechanisms exist, this threat may be reduced.

title: Students may be unaware of the full extent of grade-record retention and use
description: This flow persists detailed grade records including feedback, grader identity, and timestamps. If students are not clearly informed that these details are stored, retained, and potentially used for appeals, analytics, accreditation, or staff oversight, the processing may be insufficiently transparent.
assumptions: Assumes privacy notices or in-context explanations may not fully describe this storage and its secondary uses.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness is inferred from the flow alone and depends on surrounding notice mechanisms not shown in the DFD.

title: Persisting detailed grade records may exceed necessity or lawful retention limits
description: The write stores multiple personal-data fields—student id, course, grade, feedback, grader id, and timestamp. If all fields are not strictly necessary for the stated educational purpose, or if records are retained longer than policy/regulation permits, the datastore can create non-compliance with data-minimization, purpose-limitation, retention, or educational-record obligations.
assumptions: Assumes applicable policies or laws constrain which grading data may be stored and for how long.
uncertainty_note: Compliance impact depends on jurisdiction and institutional policy; exact tree-node naming may vary by LINDDUN version.

title: Request processing requires identified student data
description: To return the correct grades and feedback, the web app must process data that identifies the student (for example a login/session identifier or student number). This creates an identifying threat if the flow collects or uses more identifying attributes than necessary for the request.
assumptions: Assumes the student is authenticated or otherwise identified so the portal can retrieve the correct records.

title: Request reveals interest in specific grades or feedback
description: The incoming request can disclose that the student is viewing their grades and feedback at a particular time. Such request metadata may reveal behavior, academic status checking patterns, or concern about a course if logged, monitored, or shared beyond what is necessary.
assumptions: Assumes request metadata, timestamps, course context, or access logs are stored or observable by the portal or supporting infrastructure.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgement; the retrieved context did not include a more specific disclosure node citation.

title: Student may be unable to deny having made the grades request
description: If the portal keeps detailed, attributable logs of the request, the student may later be unable to plausibly deny accessing their grades or feedback. This can be a privacy issue where strong evidence of the student's actions is retained without clear necessity or safeguards.
assumptions: Assumes the system records request logs linked to the student's identity.
uncertainty_note: Threat applicability depends on the existence and retention of attributable audit logs for this flow.

title: Portal may be unaware or insufficiently transparent about request-data handling
description: When the student requests grades and feedback, they may not be adequately informed about what request data is collected, how access logs are used, or how long such data is retained. Lack of transparency reduces user awareness for this flow.
assumptions: Assumes the portal does not clearly communicate logging, monitoring, or retention practices for grade-access requests.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgement; specific awareness-node citation was not present in the retrieved context.

title: Request processing may exceed necessity or stated purpose
description: The portal may collect or retain more data from the student's request than is necessary to serve grades and feedback, such as excessive identifiers, detailed device data, or long-lived access logs. This creates a non-compliance risk with data minimization, purpose limitation, or retention obligations.
assumptions: Assumes applicable privacy requirements mandate minimization, limited retention, and clear purpose for processing request and log data.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgement; specific non-compliance node citation was not present in the retrieved context.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grades or feedback to the wrong recipient
description: The portal may display a student's grades and teacher feedback to someone other than the intended student due to broken access control, session mix-up, insecure caching, or misaddressed response handling. This directly exposes personal educational data on this flow from the process to the external entity.
assumptions: The grades and feedback are personal data and should only be shown to the authenticated, authorized student.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement for disclosure on a process-to-external-entity flow; the retrieved context confirms threat-type applicability but did not provide the exact node.

title: Student is not adequately informed about what grade-related data is shown and why
description: The portal may present grades and teacher feedback without sufficient notice about data provenance, update timing, calculation context, retention, or who can see the information. Lack of transparency can prevent the student from understanding the processing of their educational data on this flow.
assumptions: The system is expected to provide context or notices sufficient for transparent processing of educational records.
uncertainty_note: Exact transparency node may vary by threat-tree version; applicability is grounded in insufficient information provided to the data subject during disclosure.

title: Displaying grades and feedback without a valid legal basis or beyond the permitted purpose
description: The portal may disclose grades or teacher feedback in a way that exceeds the original educational purpose, violates institutional policy, or lacks an appropriate legal basis or authorization. Even when sent to the student, the disclosure content or timing could be non-compliant if unnecessary or not properly governed.
assumptions: Compliance obligations apply to educational records, including purpose limitation and lawful processing requirements.
uncertainty_note: This is a governance/compliance threat inferred from the nature of student records rather than a specific stated policy in the prompt.

title: Grades and feedback can be linked with other portal data to profile the student
description: The grades portal may present grade and feedback information together with identifiers, course history, timestamps, or other account data, enabling linkage and inference about the student's performance, behavior, or special circumstances beyond what is necessary for simple grade viewing.
assumptions: The portal view may include identifiers or metadata in addition to the core grade content.
uncertainty_note: Inference/linkability risk depends on what surrounding metadata is displayed; the prompt only states grades and feedback are displayed.

title: Portal processes identified parent and child account data during grade request
description: When the parent logs in and requests a child's grades, the web app processes directly identifying account data and the parent-child linkage needed to retrieve the correct student's records. This creates an identifying threat because the flow inherently reveals and uses the identities of both the parent and the associated child.
assumptions: The portal uses authenticated parent accounts and stores or resolves an explicit relationship between parent and child accounts.

title: Parent login and grade request can be linked to a specific child over time
description: Repeated login and grade-request messages from the same parent account allow the web app to link multiple actions, sessions, and access patterns to the same parent and to the same linked child. This can expose behavioral patterns such as frequency of monitoring or periods of academic concern.
assumptions: The application maintains account identifiers, session identifiers, or logs that correlate repeated requests over time.
uncertainty_note: Threat-tree node id chosen by best judgement; retrieved context did not include a linkability tree excerpt.

title: Grade request discloses sensitive educational information about a child
description: This flow causes the web app to receive and act on a request for a child's grades, which are personal educational records. Even before response data is returned, the request itself reveals that a specific parent is seeking a specific child's academic information, exposing sensitive relationship and education-related context inside the system.
assumptions: Children's grades are treated as personal and potentially sensitive educational data, and the request identifies which child's records are being sought.
uncertainty_note: Threat-tree node id chosen by best judgement; retrieved context did not include a detectability/disclosure tree excerpt.

title: Insufficient consent or authorization basis for parent-child data linkage
description: The web app relies on a parent account being linked to a child account to process the grade request. If that linkage is established without proper consent, legal authority, or age-appropriate governance, the system may process the child's educational data in a way that does not comply with privacy expectations or applicable regulation.
assumptions: Compliance obligations require a valid basis and correctly managed authorization for parent access to a child's educational records.
uncertainty_note: This is a genuine risk for this flow, but the exact tree node id is selected by best judgement because the retrieved context did not provide non-compliance tree details.

title: Parent may later deny having requested the child's grades
description: If the portal does not maintain privacy-appropriate but reliable records of authentication and requests, a parent could deny having initiated a grade lookup, making it difficult to establish accountability for access to the child's records.
assumptions: The system needs an audit trail of authenticated access requests to educational records.
uncertainty_note: Threat-tree node id chosen by best judgement; retrieved context did not include a non-repudiation tree excerpt.

title: Parent can infer broader child performance patterns from detailed grade history
description: Displaying grades, teacher feedback, and submission history to the parent may expose more information than is necessary for a specific parental purpose, enabling inference of the child's learning difficulties, behavior patterns, or special support needs from longitudinal academic details.
assumptions: Assumes the portal presents detailed historical records and free-text feedback rather than only a minimal progress summary.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-judgment because the retrieved context confirms applicability by threat type for Process→ExternalEntity flows but does not provide specific threat-tree node ids.

title: Unauthorized parent or household member could access a child's academic records
description: If the portal displays the child's grades and submission history to the wrong parent account, a former guardian, or another person using the parent's session or device, the child becomes identifiable together with sensitive academic information.
assumptions: Assumes risks such as weak session handling, shared devices, or inaccurate guardian-to-student authorization relationships.
uncertainty_note: Specific node id is assigned by best judgment; mapping-table context only establishes that detectability threats apply to this flow type.

title: Portal may disclose excessive academic details to the parent
description: Showing full feedback text and complete submission history may disclose more personal data about the child than is necessary, especially where only current attainment or attendance status is needed. Teacher comments can also reveal sensitive contextual details about health, behavior, or home circumstances.
assumptions: Assumes data minimization and role-based view restrictions are not strictly enforced for parent-facing displays.
uncertainty_note: Threat-tree node id is approximate; the context supports disclosure as applicable on the flow but does not enumerate the subtree.

title: Parent may be unaware of the extent and purpose of academic data shown
description: The portal may present grades, feedback, and submission history without clearly informing the parent and child why each category is shown, how long it remains visible, and whether all comments are intended for parental access. This creates a privacy risk through insufficient transparency and predictability of processing.
assumptions: Assumes the interface lacks clear notices or contextual explanations for displayed data categories.
uncertainty_note: Applicability is plausible for this display flow, but exact subtree citation is best-judgment due to missing node-level context.

title: Displaying detailed student records to parents may exceed consent or legal-authority boundaries
description: The flow may conflict with consent, custody, age-of-child, or educational privacy constraints if the system shows detailed grades or feedback to a parent who is not legally entitled to see all of it, or if the child has rights limiting such disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes there may be jurisdiction-specific rules, custody restrictions, or mature-minor rights affecting parental visibility.
uncertainty_note: This is a compliance-oriented threat inferred from the nature of the parent-facing disclosure; exact legal applicability depends on jurisdiction and governance rules.

title: Administrative account-management actions can reveal sensitive family and role relationships to unauthorized parties
description: This flow carries names, emails, roles, and parent-child links from the school administrator into the grades portal. If the web app does not properly restrict who can view submitted account-management requests or resulting records, sensitive role assignments and family relationships could be exposed beyond authorized staff.
assumptions: The portal stores or displays the submitted account/linkage data to internal users or services, and access control may be imperfect.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement for information disclosure on a data flow; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree labeling may vary.

title: Administrative submissions identify specific students, parents, and staff through account and linkage data
description: Creating or modifying accounts and parent-child links inherently transmits directly identifying data such as names and email addresses, and associates them with roles and relationships. Anyone with access to this flow or its endpoints could identify the involved individuals.
assumptions: The data in transit or at the receiving process is accessible to some actors, logs, or monitoring components beyond the submitting administrator.
uncertainty_note: This is an inherent identifiability risk of the flow content rather than necessarily a defect; included because the flow contains direct identifiers.

title: Parent-child linkage updates enable linking of identities across family and school-role contexts
description: The flow explicitly manages parent-child relationships together with names, emails, and roles. This allows records about a parent, child, and school account to be linked across contexts, potentially revealing household composition or correlating users across otherwise separate accounts.
assumptions: The portal or connected systems can correlate submitted relationship updates with existing student, parent, and staff records.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id for linkability is estimated from general LINDDUN structure.

title: Changes to account roles and family relationships may occur without clear notice to affected users
description: When an administrator creates, changes, or disables accounts and parent-child links, affected parents, students, or staff may be unaware that their roles, account status, or family associations have changed in the portal. Lack of transparency about these updates undermines user awareness of how their personal data is being processed.
assumptions: The system may not automatically notify affected users about administrative changes to their accounts or linked relationships.
uncertainty_note: Applies if the portal lacks user-facing notification or visibility for admin-initiated account changes.

title: Administrative management of account and relationship data may exceed consent or legal authorization
description: Names, emails, roles, and especially parent-child links are personal data whose creation, modification, or disabling may require a clear legal basis, school policy basis, or consent framework. If the portal allows administrators to alter these relationships without verifying authorization or purpose limitation, processing may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Applicable privacy obligations require that relationship and account management be limited to authorized educational purposes and properly governed.
uncertainty_note: This depends on jurisdiction, school policy, and whether the system enforces authorization and purpose limitation.

title: Administrator and portal may be unable to prove who created, changed, or disabled accounts and links
description: If the receiving web app does not preserve trustworthy audit records for this flow, the school administrator could later deny making specific account or parent-child link changes, or the system could be unable to demonstrate that a specific administrative action occurred. This affects accountability for sensitive personal-data changes.
assumptions: Audit logging, actor attribution, timestamps, and integrity protection for admin actions may be incomplete or absent.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is based on best judgement for non-repudiation threats on a flow.

title: Relationship-link updates enable linking of student and parent identities
description: When the grading service writes account records together with parent-child relationship links into the account directory, the flow creates or updates explicit associations between multiple data subjects. If these links are stored more broadly than necessary or become accessible for secondary use, individuals can be linked across roles and records, revealing family relationships and enrollment associations.
assumptions: The account directory stores identifiers for both student and parent accounts and preserves the parent-child linkage written by the grading service.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best-fit LINDDUN Pro linkage semantics; exact subtree numbering may vary by version.

title: Directory entries can identify students and parents directly
description: The written account records in the directory likely contain direct identifiers or stable account identifiers for students and parents. Persisting these identifiers in a central directory makes data subjects identifiable to parties with access to the store and can facilitate lookups of specific children and guardians.
assumptions: Account records include names, usernames, email addresses, internal IDs, or other stable identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Exact field contents are not provided, but account directories commonly contain direct or persistent identifiers.

title: Stored account and family-link records may disclose sensitive relationship data
description: The directory stores not only account records but also parent-child links. Unauthorized or excessive access to this stored data can disclose personal information such as a child's association with a parent or guardian, school participation context, and household structure.
assumptions: The directory is accessible to multiple services, admins, or support personnel beyond the grading function.
uncertainty_note: This threat depends on the sensitivity and accessibility of the directory contents, which are only partially described.

title: Insufficient proof of who wrote or changed account relationship records
description: If the grading service writes account records and parent-child links without strong audit evidence, administrators or system operators may later be unable to prove which process instance created, modified, or overwrote a relationship. This weakens accountability for privacy-impacting changes to directory data.
assumptions: Write operations to the directory may lack tamper-evident logging, request attribution, or change history.
uncertainty_note: Applies if auditability of write operations is weak; the flow description does not state whether robust logging exists.

title: Directory contents may be used without subjects' awareness
description: Students and parents may not expect that grading operations populate or update a central account directory with parent-child relationship links. If this secondary storage and use is not transparent, data subjects may be unaware of how their relationship data is processed and shared across the system.
assumptions: The account directory is separate from the immediate grading context and notices may not clearly explain this write path.
uncertainty_note: This is a transparency/awareness concern inferred from the architecture; actual user notices are not described.

title: Repurposing directory relationship data for broader account management may exceed user expectations
description: Parent-child relationship links written for grading-related purposes could later be used by other services supported by the account directory, such as communications, analytics, access control, or profile management. Such broader use can make processing purposes unclear or exceed the purpose understood by students and parents.
assumptions: Other components consume the directory as a shared source of account and relationship data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness/content-expectation threat; exact LINDDUN subtree numbering may differ by catalog version.

title: Writing parent-child links to the central directory may violate data minimization or purpose-limitation obligations
description: Persisting family relationship links in the account directory may collect or retain more personal data than is necessary for grading alone, especially if the directory serves multiple system functions. Without a clear legal basis, retention limit, and constrained purpose, this flow can create non-compliance risks under privacy regulations and internal policy.
assumptions: The directory acts as a shared, longer-lived store and relationship links are retained beyond the immediate grading transaction.
uncertainty_note: Compliance assessment depends on jurisdiction, notices, legal basis, and retention policy, which are not provided.

title: Excessive third-party disclosure via full backup replication
description: The nightly replication sends full grade records, assignments, and the entire account directory to the cloud hosting provider. This may disclose more personal data than is strictly necessary for hosting/backup purposes, violating data minimization if a reduced, segmented, or pseudonymized backup would suffice.
assumptions: Assumes the cloud hosting provider is a distinct third party for privacy analysis and that all replicated records contain personal data about students and staff.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement for third-party/purpose-overbroad disclosure; exact subtree labeling may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Sensitive educational data disclosed to hosting provider
description: Full grade records and assignment content can reveal highly sensitive information about individuals' academic performance, behavior, and identity. Replicating these datasets to an external hosting provider expands the set of parties able to access or infer this information.
assumptions: Assumes the provider can access data in at least some operational scenarios (e.g., managed storage, support, administration, legal access, or compromise of provider environment).
uncertainty_note: Exact node id may differ across threat-tree editions; grounded in clear cross-boundary disclosure of personal and potentially sensitive data.

title: Cross-dataset linkability enabled by consolidated backup
description: By shipping grade records, assignments, and the account directory together in one replicated backup, the flow creates a unified dataset that makes it easier for the hosting provider or anyone with access there to link identities to coursework and performance across contexts.
assumptions: Assumes the replicated backup preserves common identifiers or relational keys across the included datasets.
uncertainty_note: Linkability clearly applies, but the exact tree node id is an informed approximation.

title: Direct identifiability through account directory in backup
description: Including the account directory alongside grades and assignments means individuals are directly identifiable within the replicated data. Names, usernames, email addresses, or student IDs can be used to attribute educational records to specific people.
assumptions: Assumes the account directory contains direct identifiers and is replicated in readable form or recoverable form.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id may vary by model version; threat is straightforward identifiability from direct identifiers.

title: Potential non-compliance with minimization and third-party transfer obligations
description: Replicating complete academic and directory datasets to a cloud provider may exceed what is necessary for backup/hosting and may trigger regulatory or contractual obligations around processor management, transfer transparency, retention, access control, and lawful basis. If these are not satisfied, the flow creates a non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes applicable education/privacy regulation or internal policy constrains third-party sharing, data minimization, retention, and international transfers.
uncertainty_note: This is a compliance-oriented threat grounded in the described transfer, but exact legal applicability depends on jurisdiction and contract details.

title: Linkability of grade records across multiple audience views
description: The grading service reads the same grade records to build student, parent, and teacher views. If P2 reuses stable identifiers or correlates records across these contexts, observers or downstream components could link a student's academic events across roles and sessions, enabling broader profiling of the student and their relationships.
assumptions: P2 generates or exposes role-specific views from a common underlying record set and uses persistent identifiers or shared metadata across those views.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgment for linkability via shared identifiers/correlated records; exact subnode may vary by the LINDDUN Pro tree version.

title: Identifiability of students from retrieved grade records
description: Because grade records are read to construct views for parents, teachers, and students, P2 necessarily processes directly identifying or readily attributable educational data. If the service includes names, student numbers, class/group context, or other strong identifiers in responses or logs, individual students can be identified from the retrieved data.
assumptions: The grade records contain student-level educational information and P2 exposes some identifiers or quasi-identifiers to render the views.
uncertainty_note: Exact subnode chosen by best judgment for direct or indirect identifiability during data retrieval and presentation.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grade information to inappropriate viewers
description: This flow supplies grade records to a service that builds views for different roles. If P2 fails to enforce role-based access control, context separation, or least-privilege filtering when reading from DS2, sensitive grade information could be disclosed to the wrong student, parent, teacher, or internal component.
assumptions: Different audiences are entitled to different subsets of grade data, and P2 is responsible for filtering or authorizing access after reading from DS2.
uncertainty_note: Threat is clearly applicable, but the exact D-tree subnode may differ depending on whether the taxonomy emphasizes access control failure, over-broad retrieval, or insecure output handling.

title: Excessive retrieval of grade records beyond what is needed for each view
description: To build several audience-specific views, P2 may read more grade data from DS2 than is necessary for the current request, such as entire student histories, comments, or records for unrelated students. This creates unnecessary dissemination and handling of personal data inside the service.
assumptions: Queries from P2 to DS2 may return superset datasets that are later filtered in memory rather than minimizing data at source.
uncertainty_note: Tree node reflects data minimization/dissemination concerns by best judgment; naming may vary across versions of the threat tree.

title: Data subjects may be unaware of role-based reuse of their grade records
description: Students and parents may not realize that the same underlying grade records are repurposed by P2 to generate multiple views for different audiences. Without clear notice, users may be unaware of how broadly their educational data is used and presented within the system.
assumptions: The system does not clearly communicate to students/parents how grade data is reused across audience-specific interfaces.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible unawareness threat grounded in multi-context reuse, though evidence about actual notice mechanisms is not provided.

title: Use of grade records for multi-party views may exceed consent or educational-purpose constraints
description: Reading grade records to build student, parent, and teacher views may be non-compliant if the system uses data beyond the purposes, legal basis, or consent scope communicated to data subjects, especially where parental access depends on age, guardianship status, or local education/privacy rules.
assumptions: Applicable policy or legal constraints limit which viewers may access grades and under what circumstances, and compliance depends on P2 implementing those constraints correctly.
uncertainty_note: Compliance applicability is strong in educational contexts, but exact obligations depend on jurisdiction and product policy; tree node id is best-effort.
